name: Shoot
description: Shoot is a banking betting game in the Red Dog family. The dealer maintains the pot while each player bets that their hidden hand contains a card of the same suit and higher rank than the dealer's turned-up card.
origin: Traditional gambling variant (documented in Red Dog family)

history.origins: Shoot is one of several named variants of the Red Dog / High Card Pool banking game family.
timeline: 20th century: Red Dog family variants are published in card-game collections.
Modern era: Shoot persists as a table gambling variant in home-rule circles.
history.cultural: Played as a social gambling game with agreed table limits and rotating dealer risk.
history.evolution: Variant rules changed around dealer stake management, number of cards dealt, and dealer-rotation conditions when the pot busts or survives.

setup.players: 3 to about 8 players, with one acting as dealer/banker.
setup.dealing: Dealer stakes the pot, then deals 3 cards to each non-dealer player. Players look at cards only just before their own bet.
setup.equipment: Cards and money/chips for a shared dealer-controlled pot.

rules.objective: Win bets from the bank by proving a same-suit higher card against the dealer's turned-up card.
rules.gameplay: Each betting turn, the active player stakes between table minimum and current pot size. Dealer reveals a card. If the player can show a card in hand of the same suit and higher rank, the player wins an equal amount from pot; otherwise the stake is lost to pot. If pot empties mid-deal, remaining players do not bet and deal passes left.
keyRules: Dealer alone funds the initial pot in Shoot.
Players are dealt only three cards each.
Pot exhaustion immediately ends remaining bets for that deal.

strategy.basic: Bet conservatively when pot is small or hand lacks strong suit-over-rank coverage.
strategy.intermediate: Adjust stake sizing to pot depth and likelihood that at least one card can beat dealer's reveal.
strategy.advanced: As dealer, manage continuation decisions over multi-deal runs based on pot volatility and table tendencies.
tips: Hand strength is suit-dependent; mixed low cards justify minimum bets.
Dealer risk grows sharply when players can bet near full-pot amounts.

scoring.description: Shoot is bankroll-based: successful bets pay from pot, failed bets feed the pot, and deal rotation depends on pot survival or bust.
scoring.winCondition: Session winner is the player/dealer position with best net profit under agreed stop condition.
